reading_decisions.why: Its three-driver taxonomy is sound and statuses are accurate, but the theme 'Changed intent can require correction despite successful execution' should exclude E04, whose pre-correction edit failed ('wrong file'), so that framing fits only E08 and E12.

Its codes match the corpus with correct statuses and it preserves unknown as unresolved rather than failure; merging failure and unknown into one theme is acceptable because the separate codes keep the distinction intact.
It adds the corpus-supported refinements that successful actions can be superseded (E08, E12) and that E04 mixes a failure with an explicit correction, both of which I adopted as memo claims.

output.what_changed_my_view: All three readings converged on the same three drivers, so I re-verified each citation against the corpus myself rather than treating agreement as proof. Reading C's observations that E08 and E12 pair succeeded events with superseding corrections, and that E04 mixes a failure with a correction, sharpened my success-supersession claim and the mixed-case exception.
